newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu cancels U.S. trip; clashes in Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu cancels U.S. trip; clashes in Hebron.

text.p: Clashes erupted in the West Bank town of Hebron on Saturday as Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu cancelled a U.S. trip in a move local media attributed to the peacemaking crisis with Palestinians.

Netanyahu's spokesmen denied the faltering peace process was the reason for the cancellation. They said impending domestic legislation demanded Netanyahu's attention and that was why he would not leave as planned on June 21 for New York.

In Hebron, Israeli troops firing rubber bullets shot and slightly wounded 20 Palestinian protesters, witnesses said. The Israeli army confirmed there were clashes in Hebron but said it did not know of any casualties.
Earlier on Saturday, Palestinian gunmen shot and wounded an Israeli woman motorist at Har Adar Jewish settlement in the West Bank north of Jerusalem, Israeli security sources said.
Tensions between Israel and the Palestinians have been high and periodically flared into violence since Israel began building a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March.

Netanyahu spokesman Ofir Akunis, asked if Netanyahu's trip had been cancelled due to pending legislation on who may perform conversions to Judaism in Israel, told Reuters: "Yes, that's true...He was to have left on June 21."
He said Netanyahu was to have gone to New York to attend U.N. functions.
A second Netanyahu aide, Shai Bazak, denied local media reports the trip was cancelled due to the deadlock in peace moves, telling Reuters: "That's not correct."
Israel's army radio said Netanyahu cancelled because he had hoped for a meeting with President Bill Clinton but now wanted to avoid talks with Clinton due to the faltering peace process.
"That (legislation) is the official excuse...The problem is that the diplomatic process is deadlocked and strongly deadlocked," the radio's diplomatic reporter Udi Segal said.
"He (Netanyahu) thought he would arrive...after a summit, after some sort of meeting with Arafat," Segal said.
On Thursday, Egyptian envoy Osama el-Baz shuttled between Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat in his latest bid to solve the impasse.

He returned to Egypt saying more work was needed to end the crisis. Palestinians demand Israel halt settlement construction before they will resume substantive negotiations. Netanyahu vows to continue building.

The Hebron clashes erupted when dozens of Palestinian youths began hurling stones and petrol bombs at Israeli troops guarding Jewish enclaves in the city of 100,000 Palestinians. Some 400 Jewish settlers live in the heavily fortified enclaves.

Several Palestinian demonstrators told Reuters they had come to confront the Israelis to protest a non-binding U.S. House of Representatives resolution on Tuesday calling on Clinton to affirm that Jerusalem must remain Israel's undivided capital.

After the shooting at Har Adar, the Israeli army set searched surrounding Palestinian villages for the attackers. It said troops arrested six residents of Biddu village. It added a curfew had been imposed on the village of Qatannah.

Palestinians say settlement building in Jerusalem pre-empts final peace talks that are to be held covering issues including the status of Jerusalem. They want Arab East Jerusalem as capital of a future state.
Israel vows never to cede any part of the city. It captured East Jerusalem in the 1967 Middle East war, and annexed it in a move unrecognised by the international community.
